currentContext.strengths: Category leadership: largest manufacturer of Gathiya in India, largest manufacturer of Snack Pellets in India, 2nd largest organised Ethnic Namkeen manufacturer in Gujarat, and 4th largest manufacturer of Papad in India|Vertically integrated, backward-integrated business model — in-house manufacturing of raw snack pellets, spices and besan, plus in-house automation and engineering for namkeen machinery and logistics vehicle customisation|Extensive distribution reach: 953 distributors, 13 states and 2 Union Territories, 294 owned logistics vehicles and 40,000 MT of in-house cold storage|Diversified product portfolio across 9 categories, 98 products and 347 SKUs, spanning multiple price points and pack sizes|Experienced, founder-led management team with a 30+ year operating history in ethnic snacking
currentContext.strategies: Distribution roadmap: deepen penetration in core markets by moving from weekly to bi-weekly servicing of existing outlets and strengthening retailer relationships; in focus markets, onboard new distributors in underserved areas to widen reach|Expand the product range through a diverse portfolio, refreshed packaging and focused brand-building, with wafers positioned as a key growth driver supported by the Modasa facility and India's largest cold storage infrastructure|Brand building served digital-first: a unified marketing approach across print, radio, digital, in-store branding and event sponsorships, alongside growing e-commerce presence through marketplace partnerships, SEO and social campaigns|Innovation and premiumisation: introduce new flavours, regional variants and premium offerings, supported by upgraded, sustainable packaging to boost shelf appeal and perceived value|Optimise technology and operational efficiency via an integrated ERP system aligning demand with production across finance, sales and inventory, ongoing supply chain/logistics upgrades, and deepening backward integration for cost efficiency and pricing competitiveness|Vertically integrated, advanced business operations: automated warehousing and material handling (conveyors, AGVs), in-house engineering/fabrication of transport containers and logistics vehicle maintenance, and in-house design/manufacture of production machinery|Maintain a dedicated R&D team focused on innovation and product diversification, which has already expanded the portfolio into noodles, tortilla chips and cheese balls, working closely with operations to ensure FSSAI compliance|The Company follows a practice of declaring multiple interim dividends through the financial year rather than a single final dividend — three interim dividends were declared and paid during FY2025-26 — and maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on the Company's website); no further detail of the policy's content is present in this bundle. The BRSR confirms the Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint-venture entities (holding/subsidiary/associate table reported as Nil), indicating capital is deployed within the standalone entity rather than through group structures.
currentContext.expansion: Gopal Snacks operates a manufacturing network of four primary facilities (Rajkot and Modasa in Gujarat, Nagpur in Maharashtra, plus a substitute Gondal facility) and three ancillary facilities (Rajkot and Modasa), with combined installed capacity of nearly 3.6 lakh MT. The Company's capacity build-out has proceeded through a 'Journey of Growth': the first major Rajkot facility (2010), a second primary facility at Nagpur with besan manufacturing (2018), additional ancillary facilities at Rajkot for raw snack pellet and spice production deepening backward integration (2019), a new primary hub at Modasa (2021), a 40,000 MT in-house cold storage facility (2022), a raw snack pellet plant at Modasa paired with a 2 MW captive windmill (2023), and in 2025 the commissioning of the new Gondal facility (initial capacity 64,995 MTPA) alongside the successful set-up and commissioning of the expanded Modasa manufacturing facility. The Modasa plant, commissioned in December 2025 with an installed capacity of 63,085 MT, restored a substantial portion of capacity impacted by the Rajkot fire, was designed with scope for gradual scale-up to support future volume growth, and enables almost the full dealer product basket (Namkeen, Gathiya, Wafers, Snack Pellets, Extruded Snacks) to be serviced from a single, centralised location with higher-capacity fryers and an ultra-modern dispatch facility, supported by a DMS implementation for supply chain management. Per the Manufacturing Infrastructure table, the Rajkot primary facility's capacity and utilisation were nullified during the year due to the fire, with Gondal operating as a substitute (not an infrastructure expansion) during the recovery period.

risks.note: Fluctuations in the cost of key inputs, particularly chana and potato, can raise production costs and squeeze profitability if not adequately hedged through stocking and procurement strategy; the Company holds forward stock (6-8 months of requirement for chana/potato, reserves currently lasting through nearly end-November) to buffer short-term price increases.

Variability in monsoon patterns and weather anomalies such as El Niño can affect crop yields and raw material availability for key agricultural commodities, adding unpredictability to input costs and supply continuity, and can also influence rural incomes and consumption patterns more broadly.

Both local and international snack brands compete aggressively on price, innovation and distribution, putting continuous pressure on market share and margins; regional champions and private-label brands add further pressure in modern trade.

Flagged as a SWOT weakness; manufacturing is concentrated in a small number of locations (Gujarat/Maharashtra), which was exposed by supply chain disruption from the Rajkot facility fire during the year, requiring a shift to third-party manufacturing and substitute capacity at Gondal/Modasa.

Potential disruptions from natural disasters, pandemics, political instability or logistical chokepoints could affect raw material availability and distribution of finished products; mitigated via geographically diversified suppliers, strategic inventory reserves, supply chain management software, and an in-house logistics fleet.
Evolving food safety standards and compliance requirements could increase operating costs or restrict certain operations if not proactively monitored and managed.

risks.risk: Narrow category focus and limited international presence
risks.note: Flagged as SWOT weaknesses; the Company's revenue remains concentrated in a relatively narrow snacks category set with limited international/export presence, constraining diversification of demand sources.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity, data privacy and data management risk
risks.note: Directors' Report lists cyber security, data management/migration risk and data privacy risk among the material risks the Company monitors as part of its risk management framework, alongside raw-material cost escalation, competitive intensity, regulatory change and environmental/climate risk.

one-line thesis: Gopal Snacks reports a strong Q4 rebound (29% YoY revenue) driven by the full stabilization of the Rajkot and Modasa facilities post-fire, shifting the narrative from supply-constrained recovery to volume-led growth in FY27. Management guides for 20-25% top-line growth and 8-9% EBITDA margins, leveraging operating leverage and logistics optimization despite persistent input cost inflation.

PAT: Rs. 29.9 Cr (Q4, 7.3% margin); Rs. 73.7 Cr (FY26, 4.9% margin). One-offs: Rs. 17.5 Cr insurance proceeds received in Q4 (Total FY26: Rs. 37.4 Cr); Remaining claim of Rs. 35-40 Cr expected in Q2FY27 based on asset restatement value. Net Debt: Elevated working capital due to chana stockpiling; Finance cost guided to rise to ~Rs. 10 Cr in FY27 (vs Rs. 7 Cr in FY26). Order Book: N/A (FMCG).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Delta of Rs. 330-350 Cr in FY27 (implied ~22-23% growth). EBITDA Margin: 8-9% for FY27 (exit run-rate near double-digit). Order Inflow: Stable demand; focus on distributor expansion (target +250 dealers in FY27). Capex: Rs. 40-45 Cr for FY27 (mostly maintenance + corporate office).
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Demand indicated by 5 lakh outlet presence and real-time DMS booking.
segment / subsidiary detail: Gathiya (Base Rs. 410 Cr, target +18-20%); Namkeen (Base Rs. 350 Cr, target +15%); Fryums (Base Rs. 250 Cr, target +15%); Wafers (Base Rs. 155 Cr, target +40%); Others/Bakery (target +30%). New products (Cupcakes, Drinks) piloted in Gujarat.
growth verticals / optionality: Focus states (non-Gujarat) targeted for Rs. 125-130 Cr growth; Quick commerce, Modern Trade, Railways targeted for Rs. 35 Cr; Core Gujarat market targeted for Rs. 170-180 Cr via double-coverage expansion (40% of beats by Q1FY27). Third-party manufacturing in UP/Chhattisgarh/South to reduce logistics costs and penetrate new geographies.
margins & cost dynamics: Input inflation (Palm oil, Packaging) up 15-20%, impacting margins by ~0.5%; mitigated via 4% grammage reduction and price hikes. RM Basket: Palm Oil (26-27%), Chana (21-22%), Laminate (18-19%), Potato (6%). Logistics cost benefit of 0.4-0.5% realized from Modasa/Rajkot integration. Trade spends to remain elevated in H1FY27 to regain share, then rationalize.
capex / expansion: Rs. 40-45 Cr planned for FY27. Major expansion capex complete. Includes new corporate office in Rajkot. Rajkot plant capacity: 105,000 MT. Gondal facility to be discontinued.
capital allocation: Debt used for working capital (chana inventory build-up). Insurance proceeds (Rs. 35-40 Cr pending) to bolster cash flows. No dividend/buyback commentary; focus on organic capacity and distribution funding.
risks & watch-items: El Nino impact on rural demand and pulse prices (Chana) in H2FY27; Persistent input cost inflation; Execution risk in focus states; Competition from unorganized sector pricing wars.
management quality / tone: Confident on volume recovery and margin expansion; Pragmatic on inflation (active mitigation via grammage/pricing); Focused on market share regain over immediate profit maximization in H1.
non-obvious takeaways: Shift in SKU mix: Rs. 5 price point share down 300 bps not due to weakness but introduction of higher-MRP jar formats (e.g., Wafer Biscuit jars); 'Others' category surged from Rs. 25 Cr to Rs. 63 Cr driven by new launches; Third-party manufacturing is a strategic logistics play, not just capacity fill.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Gopal Snacks is a vertically integrated Indian ethnic-snacks manufacturer and the largest producer of Gathiya in India, with a diversified namkeen, snack-pellet, wafer, papad, besan and spices portfolio sold through an extensive general-trade distribution network.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Gopal Snacks Limited manufactures and markets ethnic Indian snacks under its own brands — gathiya, namkeen, wafers, papad, snack pellets, besan and spices, plus a smaller basket of grocery, bakery, edible oil, confectionary and beverage items — sold through general trade, modern trade and e-commerce across 13 states and 2 Union Territories in India and a small number of export markets. The Company runs a vertically integrated, backward-integrated model, manufacturing its own raw snack pellets, spices and besan, supported by six manufacturing facilities (including three ancillary units), in-house cold storage and an owned logistics fleet.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's FMCG sector growth is expected to stay steady, with revenue rising 100-200 basis points to 6-8%, supported by stable rural demand and a revival in urban markets (per IBEF)
- Rural India is expected to contribute 51% of affordable premium volumes by 2030 (up from 45% in 2021), with rural markets also leading premium FMCG growth; volume growth is expected to come from rural India while value growth comes from urban India
- Demand patterns vary by consumer group: urban segments lean toward premiumisation while price-sensitive markets stay value-conscious, requiring disciplined price-pack architecture and portfolio strategy
- FMCG growth is being driven by gradual improvement in real incomes, steady demand for staples and everyday essentials, and sustained consumer focus on health, hygiene, convenience and value
- General trade remains the dominant channel, but modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce are gaining further ground, especially in urban areas
- Input costs remain uneven: easing headline inflation is being partly offset by volatility in food commodities and energy-linked inputs
- Company-specific: Focus State sales rose steadily from Rs. 89.6 crore in FY23 to Rs. 100.1 crore in FY26, reflecting growing market penetration
- Company-specific: sales of larger pack sizes grew from Rs. 230.4 crore in FY25 to Rs. 285.1 crore in FY26, a rise of Rs. 54.7 crore, reflecting deepening consumer trust and rising disposable incomes
- Company-specific: wafers are considered one of the fastest-growing categories in Indian snacking, fuelled by rising demand for convenient, affordable and flavourful options, positioning the Company to capture greater market share as the segment expands

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input inflation (Palm oil, Packaging) up 15-20%, impacting margins by ~0.5%; mitigated via 4% grammage reduction and price hikes. RM Basket: Palm Oil (26-27%), Chana (21-22%), Laminate (18-19%), Potato (6%). Logistics cost benefit of 0.4-0.5% realized from Modasa/Rajkot integration. Trade spends to remain elevated in H1FY27 to regain share, then rationalize.

capital_allocation.body: Debt used for working capital (chana inventory build-up). Insurance proceeds (Rs. 35-40 Cr pending) to bolster cash flows. No dividend/buyback commentary; focus on organic capacity and distribution funding.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Gopal Snacks operates a manufacturing network of four primary facilities (Rajkot and Modasa in Gujarat, Nagpur in Maharashtra, plus a substitute Gondal facility) and three ancillary facilities (Rajkot and Modasa), with combined installed capacity of nearly 3.6 lakh MT. The Company's capacity build-out has proceeded through a 'Journey of Growth': the first major Rajkot facility (2010), a second primary facility at Nagpur with besan manufacturing (2018), additional ancillary facilities at Rajkot for raw snack pellet and spice production deepening backward integration (2019), a new primary hub at Modasa (2021), a 40,000 MT in-house cold storage facility (2022), a raw snack pellet plant at Modasa paired with a 2 MW captive windmill (2023), and in 2025 the commissioning of the new Gondal facility (initial capacity 64,995 MTPA) alongside the successful set-up and commissioning of the expanded Modasa manufacturing facility. The Modasa plant, commissioned in December 2025 with an installed capacity of 63,085 MT, restored a substantial portion of capacity impacted by the Rajkot fire, was designed with scope for gradual scale-up to support future volume growth, and enables almost the full dealer product basket (Namkeen, Gathiya, Wafers, Snack Pellets, Extruded Snacks) to be serviced from a single, centralised location with higher-capacity fryers and an ultra-modern dispatch facility, supported by a DMS implementation for supply chain management. Per the Manufacturing Infrastructure table, the Rajkot primary facility's capacity and utilisation were nullified during the year due to the fire, with Gondal operating as a substitute (not an infrastructure expansion) during the recovery period.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on volume recovery and margin expansion; Pragmatic on inflation (active mitigation via grammage/pricing); Focused on market share regain over immediate profit maximization in H1.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Category leadership: largest manufacturer of Gathiya in India, largest manufacturer of Snack Pellets in India, 2nd largest organised Ethnic Namkeen manufacturer in Gujarat, and 4th largest manufacturer of Papad in India
- Vertically integrated, backward-integrated business model — in-house manufacturing of raw snack pellets, spices and besan, plus in-house automation and engineering for namkeen machinery and logistics vehicle customisation
- Extensive distribution reach: 953 distributors, 13 states and 2 Union Territories, 294 owned logistics vehicles and 40,000 MT of in-house cold storage
- Diversified product portfolio across 9 categories, 98 products and 347 SKUs, spanning multiple price points and pack sizes
- Experienced, founder-led management team with a 30+ year operating history in ethnic snacking

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: El Nino impact on rural demand and pulse prices (Chana) in H2FY27; Persistent input cost inflation; Execution risk in focus states; Competition from unorganized sector pricing wars.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Shift in SKU mix: Rs. 5 price point share down 300 bps not due to weakness but introduction of higher-MRP jar formats (e.g., Wafer Biscuit jars); 'Others' category surged from Rs. 25 Cr to Rs. 63 Cr driven by new launches; Third-party manufacturing is a strategic logistics play, not just capacity fill.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Distribution roadmap: deepen penetration in core markets by moving from weekly to bi-weekly servicing of existing outlets and strengthening retailer relationships; in focus markets, onboard new distributors in underserved areas to widen reach
- Expand the product range through a diverse portfolio, refreshed packaging and focused brand-building, with wafers positioned as a key growth driver supported by the Modasa facility and India's largest cold storage infrastructure
- Brand building served digital-first: a unified marketing approach across print, radio, digital, in-store branding and event …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation (Palm oil +15-20%) and supply chain disruption recovery | Gopal Snacks Limited | beneficiary | High | Full-year benefit of Rajkot/Modasa capacity, guided 20%+ volume growth, and operational leverage should drive EBITDA margin expansion from 6.7% to 8-9% despite inflation. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Fire incident] A fire at the Rajkot facility in December 2024 disrupted the business; the deck's recovery timeline runs from immediate third-party manufacturing, to commissioning Gondal, to ~80% of affected supplies recovered by February 2025, to the Rajkot Main plant recommencing operations in the current quarter.
- [Reporting basis] The covering letter states these are "Unaudited Standalone Financial Results" for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 — the deck carries no consolidated figures.
- [Micro-distributor channel] A separate SS/SSD micro-distributor layer of 135 appointees was created specifically "to mitigate supply chain disruption" and is excluded from the headline 1,007 distributor count.
- [Input risk] Management explicitly links the quarter's raw material environment to "geopolitical tensions in middle east", relevant given palmolein oil is a lead input.
